title: Junta Bombing Runs Destroy Half of Kaung Tong Village After Bhamo Vessel Losses
detail: Following the loss of six Military Commission vessels to a KIA-led ambush near Sawati on September 13, junta Y-12 aircraft and fighter jets carried out retaliatory bombing runs against Sawati, Kaung Tong and Nyaung Pin Thar villages in Kachin State that continued into September 14, 2026. Roughly half of Kaung Tong village was reportedly destroyed by fire as a result of the strikes.

media.caption: MoeMaKa CDM domestic news digest reporting continued junta retaliatory bombing of Kaung Tong village.

title: KIA-Led Forces Sink Junta Vessel in Second Defile of the Ayeyarwady Near Nat Myet Hna Taung
detail: A Military Commission vessel travelled downstream from Bhamo under cover of darkness on the night of September 13, 2026, and was attacked below Su Put Kone village before continuing to drift downstream. KIA-led forces attacked it again near Nat Myet Hna Taung, in the second defile of the Ayeyarwady River, at around 7:00 a.m. on September 14, setting it on fire and sinking it. Several senior officers — including a deputy commander of Military Operations Command 21, a G2 officer, and a battalion commander from Light Infantry Battalion 320 — reportedly escaped to shore by boat.

media.caption: MoeMaKa CDM domestic news digest reporting the September 14 vessel sinking near Nat Myet Hna Taung.

title: Junta Artillery Wounds Two Civilians Near Lu Myan Village, Waingmaw Township, in KIA Interception
detail: Around 9:00 a.m. on Monday, September 14, 2026, KIA-led forces intercepted a junta military column near Lu Myan village, about seven miles east of Waingmaw Township, Kachin State. Junta forces responded with artillery and shellfire; shells struck the neighboring village of Wu Yang, wounding two civilian men, one critically. A KIA officer, Col. Naw Bu, said the clash itself was brief but the shellfire was intense — part of what remains the fiercest of three active Kachin State battlefronts around Bhamo.

media.caption: Myanmar Now report on continued fighting around Bhamo, including the Sept 14 shelling near Lu Myan village.
